top_stories.title: In the agentic era, standing privilege must go: Key thoughts from the SailPoint Navigate keynote
top_stories.summary: At Navigate 2026 in Austin, SailPoint outlined a strategic shift toward real-time access prevention, moving beyond traditional identity governance to address agentic AI era challenges. The keynote emphasized eliminating standing privileges as a core tenet of their evolving platform direction.

top_stories.title: SailPoint adds AI agent discovery, temporary access and compliance automation
top_stories.summary: SailPoint has announced new capabilities including AI agent discovery, temporary access controls, and compliance automation across its SailPoint Agentic Fabric and SailPoint Human Fabric products. The updates are built on the SailPoint Atlas platform and aim to give enterprises greater visibility and governance over both human and non-human identities.

top_stories.title: OAuth grants pile up faster than you can review them. Here's how to keep up.
top_stories.summary: The article addresses the growing security risk of unreviewed OAuth grants connecting SaaS apps, AI agents, and other tools, citing the Klue breach as a real-world example of attackers exploiting forgotten OAuth grants. The piece covers why OAuth grant risks are difficult to manage and how security teams can keep up with their proliferation.

top_stories.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
top_stories.summary: Citrix has released patches for CVE-2026-107406, a critical memory overflow vulnerability in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that can enable remote code execution or denial-of-service. The flaw is specifically triggered under SAML deployment configurations, making it directly relevant to organizations using these products for federated authentication and SSO.

top_stories.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials
top_stories.summary: The FBI and Secret Service warned that the FortiBleed campaign remains active, having harvested 86,644 credentials from Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage on internet-facing Fortinet devices.

news.title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
news.summary: The PCI Security Standards Council has published advisory guidance on AI security in payment environments, covering governance, deployment, and access controls. The document includes recommendations for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data and addresses how existing PCI standards apply to AI systems.

news.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
news.summary: The FBI and agencies from six other countries reported that hackers linked to Chinese cybersecurity firm Integrity Technology Group stole emails from government, law enforcement, healthcare, and religious organizations in Southeast Asia. The group operated a portal allowing third parties to access stolen email data, and Integrity Technology Group has been sanctioned by the U.S. and UK.

news.title: ASOS links data breach to social engineering attack, credential theft
news.summary: ASOS suffered a data breach resulting from a social engineering attack and credential theft, with hackers accessing some customer personal data. The company is notifying affected customers about the cybersecurity incident.

news.title: U.S. Offers Up to $10 Million for Tips on Zhang Yu, Charged in HAFNIUM Hacks
news.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information on Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in connection with the 2021 HAFNIUM Microsoft Exchange Server attacks. The HAFNIUM campaign exploited critical vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server, compromising tens of thousands of organizations' email and identity infrastructure worldwide.

news.title: The people who know passkeys best are still typing passwords
news.summary: A Yubico and Okta survey of 1,890 technology and security professionals across nine countries found that 43% still use username and password as their primary sign-in method despite 87% reporting familiarity with passkeys. The data highlights a gap between passkey awareness and adoption among the professionals most expected to implement modern authentication.

news.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
news.summary: SonicWall released hotfixes addressing four vulnerabilities in its SMA1000 appliances, including a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF flaw. The critical flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to send requests through the secure access gateway appliance to reach internal network functions.

news.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
news.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a human-operated phishing platform that impersonates advertising portals for major AI chatbots including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to steal credentials and MFA codes. The platform lures victims with fake services like campaign optimization and spend audits, targeting business accounts to capture authentication data.

news.title: Browser-in-browser attacks use fake Meta Muse Ad lure to steal credentials
news.summary: A browser-in-browser phishing attack has been identified that uses fake Meta Muse advertisements as lures to steal user credentials. The attack technique renders a convincing fake browser window within the real browser to deceive users into entering their login information on what appears to be a legitimate page.

news.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude imitated in fake ads that steal credentials and MFA codes
news.summary: Cybercriminals are running fake advertisements impersonating ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to steal credentials and MFA codes from victims. The campaign specifically targets advertiser accounts that have preloaded credit cards and funds, making credential and MFA theft the central attack mechanism.

news.title: Half of Cybersecurity Pros Still Rely on Passwords Despite Security Concerns
news.summary: A Yubico survey found that half of cybersecurity professionals still rely on passwords as a primary authentication method despite awareness of associated security risks. The survey highlights a gap between knowledge of more secure authentication methods and actual enterprise adoption of those alternatives.

news.title: High Awareness, Low Adoption: New Survey Reveals Nearly Half of Security Professionals Still Rely on Passwords
news.summary: A joint survey by Yubico and Okta found that nearly half of security professionals still rely on passwords despite high awareness of stronger authentication methods. The study highlights an execution gap in enterprise security adoption of modern identity controls and passwordless authentication.

news.title: Stop Hoping for Secure AI and Start Building It: RSA Agent ID Closes the Agentic Identity Gap for Highly Regulated Industries
news.summary: RSA has launched Agent ID, a product designed to address identity and authentication challenges for AI agents operating in highly regulated industries such as finance and government. The solution focuses on registering AI agents, establishing authority verification for actions taken by those agents, and supporting sovereign deployment options.

news.title: Welcome to the Jungle: What We Found Inside 15,465 Public MCP Servers
news.summary: OX Security researchers analyzed 15,465 public MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and found critical vulnerabilities in the ecosystem. The research focuses on security weaknesses in AI agent infrastructure, touching on authentication and access control issues within MCP server deployments.

news.title: SailPoint’s 40x Gap — Enterprise AI Agent Adoption Has Outrun Identity Security by a Factor of 40
news.summary: SailPoint's Navigate 2026 conference in Austin revealed data showing enterprise AI agent adoption has outpaced identity security measures by a factor of 40. The findings highlight a significant gap between AI agent deployment speeds and the identity governance controls organizations have in place to secure them.

news.title: Improving SPIRE security and resiliency with AWS managed services
news.summary: The article covers improving SPIRE (SPIFFE Runtime Environment) security and resiliency using AWS managed services for workload identity in cloud environments. SPIRE is an open-source implementation of the SPIFFE standard for workload identity and authentication in machine-to-machine communication, replacing traditional static credentials like API keys and shared secrets.

news.title: Identity-aware AI data agents with AWS Lake Formation and Trusted Identity Propagation
news.summary: AWS has introduced an approach combining Lake Formation and Trusted Identity Propagation to enable identity-aware AI data agents that enforce existing access governance policies. The solution allows AI agents to respect user-level authorization controls when querying lakehouse data, propagating the end user's identity through the agent layer rather than granting the agent broad data access.

news.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini Sites steal advertising accounts, MFA codes
news.summary: A malicious campaign is targeting advertising account managers using fake AI tool websites (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity) to steal login credentials and MFA codes via browser-in-browser attacks. The attack method specifically bypasses multi-factor authentication by intercepting codes in real time through spoofed browser windows.

news.title: When identity isn’t human: securing the agentic enterprise
news.summary: The article addresses securing AI agents (non-human identities) within enterprise environments through identity governance and runtime controls. It focuses on continuous identity management and authorization frameworks applied to agentic AI systems, which represent an emerging challenge in IAM.

news.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
news.summary: Kiteworks and Citrix both faced zero-day vulnerability incidents, with Kiteworks instructing customers to power down its data-protection platform during a nine-hour maintenance window. Citrix declined to comment on reported active attacks prior to releasing a patch, highlighting differing vendor approaches to zero-day disclosure and response.

news.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
news.summary: A vulnerability in SWIFT banking and government middleware enables remote code execution (RCE). The flaw can be exploited to bypass hardware-based MFA in high-security environments, with patching recommended as the mitigation.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The update is notable for its scale, with Microsoft attributing accelerated vulnerability discovery to AI assistance.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web identity theft service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Connor Riley Moucka, a 26-year-old Canadian, pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The attacks involved unauthorized access to Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in the theft of data including over 100 million AT&T customer call and text records.
